correct_answer: Use actual FY24 rates for Aug-Nov 2024 and FPRA for December forward; the proposal must be self-corrected downward to approximately $461K before the ACO identifies the discrepancy
rationale: The correct answer is A. The Dec 2018 DFARS 252.243-7002 clause incorporated at contract award requires rates 'in effect at the time the work was performed.' For the Aug-Nov 2024 period, the work has been performed and actual (final) indirect rates are now available (certified Feb 2025). These must be used per the applicable DFARS version. For December 2024 onward (forward work), FPRA rates are appropriate because actuals are not yet determined. The Teams conversation between Holloway and Castellano reveals this is a CAS 401 (consistency) issue requiring self-correction. Answer B is wrong because it ignores the DFARS clause requirement and the availability of actual rates for completed work. Answer C applies the wrong DFARS version — the GovWin internal note explicitly confirms the PCO ruled that the Jan 2024 revision does NOT apply to this contract. Answer D goes too far: using actuals for December forward work is inappropriate because those actuals won't be final until after FY25 close. The bifurcation approach (actuals for performed work, FPRA for forward) is the correct methodology under the applicable clause version, and self-correction is mandatory under CAS 401 to avoid a consistency violation that could escalate to a DCAA finding.
